themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, etc.) spiked to 18 this week versus a baseline of 1.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—an 860% jump with z-score of 12.71—suggesting a sudden operational or enforcement change affecting Washington Heights residents.
evidence: 18 for-hire vehicle complaints this week vs. 1.9 weekly average (860% increase, z-score: 12.71)
Represents most dramatic single-week spike across all tracked complaint categories
No prior context in community board requests or local news, suggesting sudden change
reporting_angles: Did TLC enforcement activity shift? Interview TLC or NYPD about surge in complaints
Are residents reporting specific behaviors (double-parking, illegal pickup zones, congestion)? Canvass complaint filers
Did a major rideshare company change operations or pricing, driving more vehicles to the neighborhood?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 18 this week from a baseline of 4.2 per week (324% increase, z-score: 11.47), marking an acute infrastructure problem that aligns with community board's long-standing requests for street/sidewalk investment.
evidence: 18 sidewalk condition complaints this week vs. 4.2 weekly average (324% increase, z-score: 11.47)
Community board has repeatedly requested street reconstruction/upgrades—listed as top budget need
Street condition complaints also elevated at 623 over 90 days, suggesting broader infrastructure decay
reporting_angles: Photograph worst sidewalk problem areas and document tripping hazards; interview residents about accidents
Examine DOB permits (364 alterations filed recently): are construction projects damaging sidewalks or blocking repairs?
Interview DDOT about repair backlog and budget constraints in Washington Heights vs. other CDs

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints reached 4 this week versus a baseline of 1.0 per week (300% increase, z-score: 4.24), coinciding with mobile food vendor complaints jumping 2300% (3 vs. 0.1 avg), suggesting potential street food vending violations or hygiene breakdown.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average (300% increase, z-score: 4.24)
3 mobile food vendor complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Vendor enforcement complaints also up 321% (10 vs. 2.4 avg), suggesting compliance or inspection gaps
reporting_angles: Interview DOHMH about enforcement actions on street vendors in Washington Heights this week; request inspection records
Locate food poisoning complaint filers and document symptoms/vendors involved; identify any clusters
Are unlicensed vendors operating unchecked? Scout high-foot-traffic areas and cross-reference with permit database

themes_detail.label: Industrial Waste Dumping
themes_detail.summary: Industrial waste complaints spiked to 3 last week from a baseline of 0.2 per week (1100% increase, z-score: 4.16), alongside lot condition complaints up 700%, indicating possible illegal dumping or construction debris violations in Washington Heights.
evidence: 3 industrial waste complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score: 4.16)
3 lot condition complaints (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 3.77)
364 DOB permits filed in 90-day window—alteration work may be generating construction debris
reporting_angles: Map industrial waste and lot condition complaint locations; visit sites to document dumping/debris
Interview NYC Department of Sanitation about enforcement against illegal waste disposal; request violation records
Cross-reference complaint addresses with active DOB permits—are construction projects failing to properly dispose waste?

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Crisis (Structural)
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints dominate the 90-day profile at 8,063 complaints—nearly 5x the next-highest category—reflecting a persistent, systemic housing crisis in Washington Heights that community boards have flagged but remains unresolved.
evidence: 8,063 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days—89% of all complaints in top 10 categories
Averages ~270 complaints per week, dwarfing noise (555/week combined) and all other categories
Structural issue flagged in recurring community board budget requests for housing authority security/upgrades
reporting_angles: Profile 2-3 families experiencing heat loss; connect to HPD complaint data and housing court eviction patterns
Interview HPD and NYCHA about enforcement against landlords with repeat violations; request violation/penalty data
Are older building stock or specific landlords responsible for majority of complaints? Data analysis could identify targets for investigation
